raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too thin this year. On my 8 mu, I will keep the land that usually does wheat-maize in wheat first and then summer maize after harvest, because that is the safest way for grain and cash. I will leave 4 mu for that rotation. Cotton takes more watching and more picking, so I will keep only 2 mu of cotton. Watermelon can bring better money if the market is good, but it also needs care and water, so I will do 2 mu, not more. With some people working off-farm, I cannot manage too much fine work, so I want a steady plan, same as what has worked around our village.

For wheat, I will sow in early October on the 4 mu after simple rotary tillage, using a local improved seed that people nearby use. I usually put fertilizer down at sowing and then add some more in spring if the wheat color is not strong. I have well water, so I will irrigate, but not too many times because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away on the same 4 mu. The turnaround is tight, so I will keep tillage simple and plant fast. Cotton and watermelon I will keep on the other 4 mu. Cotton gives me some cash, but too much cotton is tiring for the family. Watermelon I plant because if the price is decent, it helps household income, but I do not want to risk too much land on it.
